opportunities.title: nft-reward: update_nft_metadata ignores the locked and MetadataFrozen states
opportunities.summary: `contracts/nft-reward/src/lib.rs:558` checks ownership and nothing else: ```rust updater.require_auth(); let mut nft = Storage::get_nft(&env, nft_id).ok_or(NftNotFound)?; if nft.owner != updater { return Err(NotOwner); } ``` `NftErrorCode::MetadataFrozen` (= 14) and `NftErrorCode::NftLocked` (= 12) both exist in `contracts/nft-reward/src/errors.rs`, and `NftData.locked` is stored per NFT. Neither is consulted. `MetadataFrozen` in particular is defined and returned from nowhere in the crate — a declared error for a feature that was never wired up. For a collectible, "the metadata can no longer change" is a meaningful guarantee to offer buyers, and right now it is offered by the error enum and delivered by nothing. **Fix** Either implement freezing — a per-NFT or per-collection frozen flag, an admin or owner entrypoint to set it, and a check in `update_nft_metadata` and `admin_update_image_uris` — or remove `MetadataFrozen` from the enum. Independently, reject metadata updates on a `locked` NFT. **Acceptance criteria** - [ ] `MetadataFrozen` is either returned by a real code path or removed. - [ ] Updating a locked NFT's metadata fails with `NftLocked`. - [ ] Tests cover both. --- _F

opportunities.title: reward-manager: fund_reward_pool rejects funding from anyone but the pool creator
opportunities.summary: `contracts/reward-manager/src/lib.rs:502-507`: ```rust if funder != pool_config.creator { return Err(RewardErrorCode::Unauthorized); } pool_config.creator.require_auth(); ``` The function takes a `funder: Address` parameter and then requires it to equal the creator — so the parameter can only ever hold one value and carries no information. This forecloses sponsorship, which is a natural fit for the product: a brand funding a community hunt, a DAO topping up a pool, several people pooling a prize. Today each of them would have to send XLM to the creator and trust them to forward it. It is also inconsistent with the refund path, which sends the whole balance to the creator — so if third-party funding were allowed, sponsors' contributions would be refundable to someone else. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
